meta.subtitle: AI optics demand has rebuilt the P&L; at $1,045.78 the price already discounts much of the consensus FY28 path

analystCommentary:
Lumentum has turned from a cyclical telecom-optics supplier into a capacity-constrained AI infrastructure name. FY26 rebuilt revenue, margins and cash flow together, and management guides the next quarter higher again.

The operating story is not in dispute; the price is. At $1,045.78 the stock trades near the top of a 52-week range that starts at $147.81, and the forward multiple already assumes the consensus revenue path for the next two fiscal years arrives on schedule.

The headline GAAP loss is an accounting charge from converting notes into stock, not an operating problem; its lasting effect is a larger share count.

We rate LITE HOLD with a $950–$1,250 target range. The bull case needs consensus delivered and a premium multiple held; the bear case needs only a repeat of the last inventory cycle.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Lumentum Holdings Inc. designs and manufactures optical and photonic products: semiconductor laser chips, laser sub-assemblies, line subsystems and wavelength management systems (Components), and optical modules, optical circuit switches and industrial lasers (Systems). Its products serve cloud, AI/ML, telecommunications, consumer and industrial markets.

During the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 the company reorganized and now reports as a single segment under one management team. It is headquartered in San Jose, California.

thesis.body: Demand for AI data center optics has lifted revenue, margins and cash generation at once, and the near-term guide extends that run. We think the shares already price most of it: our scenario-weighted value sits essentially at the current price (see Valuation), while the downside if AI spending pauses is deep. The reward/risk does not clear our BUY bar.

catalysts: Delivery against the first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue and margin guide.
Ramp of optical circuit switches and next-generation cloud modules.
Early in-rack optics orders turning into volume.
Capacity additions that loosen the current supply allocation.
risks: An AI capex pause or customer inventory correction, the pattern that cut FY24 revenue.
Dependence on a small number of large customers.
Tariffs and export controls on a global manufacturing footprint.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY26 revenue was $3.01 billion, up {+83.2%+} from $1.6 billion in FY25. GAAP gross margin rose to 41.7% from 28.0%, and GAAP operating margin reached 17.4% after three years of losses.

The fourth quarter carried the acceleration. Net revenue was $1.01 billion, up from $808.4 million in Q3 and $480.7 million in Q4 FY25. The vendor quarterly series in the Facts block shows Q4'26 revenue growth of +51.2%, while the press release reports {+109.3%+} year over year; the two disagree, and we use the press release. Q4 GAAP gross margin was 47.4% (non-GAAP 50.4%) and GAAP operating margin 27.8% (non-GAAP 36.6%).

The GAAP net loss of $6.9 billion, or $92.96 per diluted share, comes from a one-time, non-cash $7.8 billion loss on debt extinguishment tied to the equitization of certain convertible notes in Q4. On a non-GAAP basis FY26 net income was $782.3 million, or $8.67 per diluted share, which is the better read of operating earnings.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Cash and short-term investments reached $2.7 billion at fiscal year-end, an increase of $1.9 billion over the year but a decrease of $433.9 million from the end of Q3.

The two debt sources disagree. The vendor Facts show total debt of $3.2B, while the press-release balance sheet shows the current portion of long-term debt at $1,596.9 million and long-term debt at $40.5 million. We use the press-release balance sheet, the company's own statement, and do not rely on the vendor net-debt figure.

On that basis, the current portion of long-term debt was up from $10.6 million a year earlier, which with higher accounts payable pulled the current ratio down to 1.68 from 4.37 in FY25. Cash still exceeds that current debt. Total equity rose to $4.6B from $1.1B as notes were equitized, and interest coverage of 24.1x leaves debt service comfortable.

Inventories and receivables both rose over the year, which fits a supply-constrained ramp but would be the first lines to strain if orders slow.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow rose to $0.8B in FY26 from $0.1B in FY25. Capital expenditure stepped up to -$451.3M as the company adds capacity, and free cash flow turned positive at $300.1M, a 10.0% FCF margin after two negative years.

Capex is the swing factor. Management says demand is outpacing supply and is investing in capacity internally and with contract manufacturers, so spending is likely to stay elevated and FCF margin will lag operating margin while capacity is built.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing numbers LITE trades at 31.1x sales. The GAAP P/E of -11.2x is distorted by the extinguishment loss and is not a usable anchor. On forward numbers the stock is 48.0x NTM earnings and 30.1x FY28E EPS of $34.73.

The Street is constructive: 27 analysts, 23 Buy, 4 Hold and 0 Sell, with a consensus target of $1,159.40 and a median of $1,186.00 inside a range of $820.00–$1,400.00. Even the consensus implies only +10.9% from here.

We have no peer multiples to benchmark against, so we value LITE on whether FY27E revenue of $6.3B and FY28E revenue of $9.7B arrive, and on what multiple holds if they do.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: New product lines layer in on schedule, capacity keeps pace, consensus FY28E EPS is met or beaten, and the market extends a premium growth multiple. That takes the stock to the top of the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: FY27E EPS of $21.78 is broadly delivered and the market keeps paying about today's 30.1x for FY28E EPS of $34.73, with modest upside as estimates firm. The shares track earnings rather than re-rate.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Hyperscaler AI spending pauses or customers digest inventory, as in the FY24 cycle. Estimates are cut and the multiple de-rates, taking the stock below the low end of the Street target range and toward the lower half of its 52-week range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries half the weight because the near-term guide and supply allocation make the next few quarters unusually visible; a miss on FY27E would need a demand break, not just execution slippage. The tails get equal weight because both are plausible over a year: the new product lines could pull FY28E forward, and the company's own history shows how quickly an inventory correction lands.

The result is a weighted fair value of $1,055 and expected upside of +0.9%, against a bear-case downside of -40.7%. The upside is small and the downside is large, which is why the rating is HOLD rather than BUY.

Our $950–$1,250 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Lumentum has reported as a single segment since a reorganization in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, but it discloses revenue by product type. Components (laser chips, laser sub-assemblies, line subsystems and wavelength management systems) generated $2,005.6 million in FY26, up 79.7%, and Systems (optical modules, optical circuit switches and industrial lasers) generated $1,008.4 million, up 90.7%. In Q4 Components were 64.5% of net revenue and Systems 35.5%. Components are the building blocks behind AI data center links; cloud modules and optical circuit switches are the newer Systems lines.

moatFactors.name: Laser and photonics technology
moatFactors.body: The company describes itself as an industry-leading provider of optical and photonic products by revenue and market share, and its laser chips sit inside customers' data center links. Its own risk factors also cite rapid technology change and intense competition, so the lead has to be re-won each product generation.

moatFactors.name: Volume manufacturing capability
moatFactors.body: Management cites its volume manufacturing capability as a base for expanding into new markets. Demand currently outpaces supply and the company is making supply-allocation decisions, which shows supply is tight rather than proving an edge. A shortage also invites customers to qualify alternative suppliers, and part of the new capacity sits at contract manufacturers.

moatFactors.name: Customer relationships
moatFactors.body: Management cites close relationships with market-leading customers built over many years. Those relationships cut both ways: they anchor demand, but they also concentrate it in a few buyers with negotiating leverage.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Technology and manufacturing know-how give Lumentum real advantages while supply is constrained, and current margins show it. Those advantages are less durable once supply catches up, as the FY24 inventory cycle showed. Durability depends on staying a generation ahead in lasers and modules while large customers retain bargaining power.

points: Near-term visibility is high. Management guides the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion of revenue, a non-GAAP operating margin of 39.5% to 40.5%, and $4.05 to $4.35 of non-GAAP diluted EPS, and says the midpoint reaches its target model more than a quarter ahead of schedule.
New product layers: management names OCS solutions and the cloud module business, where it is advancing 1.6T adoption, as key growth drivers that are beginning to layer in.

In-rack optics: the CEO cites increasing demand for ultra-high-power CPO lasers, an initial order for ELS modules and a breadth of NPO engagements as the first signs that optics are starting to penetrate in-rack connectivity.
The Street expects FY27E revenue of $6.3B, up about 110%, and FY28E revenue of $9.7B. Those estimates leave little room for a supply or demand stumble.
Longer-dated options: the MD&A says LiDAR and in-cabin 3D sensing will over time significantly add to the long-term market opportunity, and industrial lasers serve precision material processing.

management.leadership: Michael Hurlston became president and CEO early in 2025, succeeding Alan Lowe, who had led the company since it became public; the October 2025 proxy describes this as the first CEO transition in the company's history and says the Board gave Mr. Hurlston a mandate to move beyond the legacy telecom business. In our view the FY26 shift toward data center optics is consistent with that mandate, though demand conditions did much of the work. The proxy also notes that Mr. Lowe had hired the entire management team and held the most critical customer relationships, which made the handoff a transition risk. Wajid Ali was executive vice president and chief financial officer at the end of fiscal year 2025, per the same proxy.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital is going into capacity, internally and with contract manufacturers, as the cash flow section shows. The company does not pay a dividend and states it does not intend to for the foreseeable future; the FY26 share-repurchase figure is not available in our data.

The key capital decision of the year was equitizing certain convertible notes. It moved a large part of the capital structure into equity and created the dilution discussed under Risks.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement dated October 2025, the board chair and CEO roles are separate, and the chair, Penelope A. Herscher, is an outside, independent director. The board determined eight directors independent under Nasdaq standards, has Audit, Compensation and Governance committees, and held 15 meetings in fiscal year 2025. The proxy reports no related-person transactions above its $120,000 threshold. In our view this leaves little governance discount to apply. The counter-reading is in the risk factors: Delaware law and the company's certificate of incorporation and bylaws contain provisions that may make a merger, tender offer or proxy contest difficult. These proxy facts predate the FY26 10-K and may have changed.
management.insiderOwnership: As of August 29, 2025, per the proxy, all directors and executive officers as a group (14 persons) beneficially owned 307,933 shares, less than 1% of the common stock. That gives insiders no blocking or control position, so outside holders carry governance. Holders of 5% or more were The Vanguard Group at 10.2% (based on a Schedule 13G/A dated February 13, 2024), FMR LLC at 9.8% and BlackRock Inc. at 8.8%. Those percentages were computed on 70,843,924 shares outstanding, before equitization lifted common shares to 88.6 million, so current stakes are lower. No single holder controls a vote.

idiosyncratic: Demand cyclicality: through FY24 customers built and then cut inventory, and FY24 revenue fell 23.1% while gross margin dropped to 18.5%. An AI spending pause would hit a company now valued for uninterrupted growth.

Customer and supplier concentration: the 10-K lists reliance on a limited number of suppliers and customers, the ability to sell to a significant customer, leverage in negotiations with large customers, and order cancellations or delays among its principal risks.
Execution on capacity: meeting guidance depends on the company and its contract manufacturers adding output on time while supply is being allocated.

Dilution: the risk factors cite dilution related to the convertible notes and the hedging activity of the 2032 Capped Call counterparties. Equitization has already raised common shares to 88.6 million from 69.8 million a year earlier, and 2.9 million preferred shares are now outstanding.
risks.systemic: Trade policy is the main external risk. The 10-K flags tariffs, export controls and trade restrictions, naming China and Thailand, and warns that tariffs may raise cost of goods sold and pressure gross margin if costs cannot be passed on. Broader macro and geopolitical conditions, including the conflicts listed in the risk factors, could slow customers' capital spending. At a high trailing sales multiple, the stock is also exposed to a market-wide de-rating of AI-linked equities, independent of company results.

body: HOLD, target range $950–$1,250. Lumentum is executing well and the near-term guide is strong, but the scenario math leaves little expected upside against a deep bear case.
We would turn more constructive on a pullback toward the low end of our target range, where the reward/risk improves, or on results that show the FY28E revenue estimate is conservative.
